The beginner assumes quantization error is roughly uniform and additive — a fixed SNR penalty per layer. The expert knows the error is structured: outlier channels in transformer hidden states (often dimensions 75, 153, and a handful of others in OPT-family models) can have magnitudes 100× the median, meaning a per-tensor INT8 scheme allocates roughly 1 effective bit to normal channels while trying to represent those outliers.
